fields.title: Branch size and a red main are habits here

sections.What we are doing instead:
Branches here are small and short-lived, because one person works one thing at a time. A red `main` gets fixed on sight, for the same reason. Both are the maintainer's habit, and no record asks for either.

[std-CI] sets the gate: every job runs on a pull request into `main`, and the branch rule makes `validate` the check a merge waits for. That stops a broken change landing. It says nothing about what happens once one has.
sections.Why we need it: A rule about branch size needs a number, and nothing here has measured one. A rule about a red `main` needs somebody other than its author to notice, and there is nobody else. Writing either without the measurement or the second person would put a clause in a standard that no reviewer could fail a change against.
sections.What compensates:
* The merge gate refuses a change that breaks a check, so a red `main` comes from a merge conflict or a flake.
* [ctl-0001] describes the branch rule, and says plainly that nothing in CI reads it.
* One maintainer works one branch at a time, so a long-running branch has nothing to diverge from.
sections.How it closes: Somebody measures how long a branch here lives and how large it gets, then writes the rule that matches. The red-`main` clause closes when a standard says what stops after a failure on `main`, and [ctl-0001] or a new control verifies it.
sections.Scope: Every branch of this repository, and `main` itself.
